messages:
marie: spotted a partner S3 package that includes a KMS-wrapped SA blob. filename: partner_bundle_2026-04-02.tgz. no clear plaintext creds but the wrapped payload references our keyRing.

josh: which env? staging/prod? any active usage seen?

marie: looks like preprod but the SA had broad roles (roles/storage.admin + roles/bigquery.dataViewer). I dumped the wrapped blob head: 
```
{"v":"1","alg":"GCP-KMS","key":"projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/ext/cryptoKeys/partner-wrap","ct":"ABCD...xyz=="}
```

liam: treat as suspected exposure. plan: immediate containment, scope, rotate, partner sync, and postmortem.

olivia: I'm oncall. will disable the SA and lock the key's IAM binding to prevent decrypt. command: `gcloud iam service-accounts disable partner-sa@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com` and `gcloud kms keys remove-iam-policy-binding partner-wrap --member='serviceAccount:partner-sa@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com' --role='roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter'`. also bump audit level for Cloud KMS+IAM.

marie: good. I'll run a repo & artifact scan across S3 buckets and GH packages for the SA email and the key path. ETA 20m.

josh: do NOT rewrap with same key material. create a new keyRing/key and rotate. we should also take a snapshot of current key versions and GC policy.

ryan: infra note: if partner uses Vault transit, we can leverage `transit/rewrap` to minimize downtime. but for wrapped blobs outside Vault we'll need a re-encrypt and replace flow. I'll prep both flows.

liam: short checklist to track in the ticket:
- [ ] disable exposed SA (owner: olivia)
- [ ] create least-priv replacement SA (owner: josh)
- [ ] create new KMS key (owner: liam)
- [ ] remove decryption binding from exposed SA (owner: olivia)
- [ ] re-encrypt artifacts and push to partner (owner: ryan)
- [ ] rotate any GH Actions / CI secrets referencing the SA (owner: marie)
- [ ] run forensic scan for exfil events (owner: marie)
- [ ] complete postmortem & policy fixes (owner: liam)

olivia: disabled SA and posted audit snapshot at `gs://redwood-audit/snapshots/1712223600.json`. sec-oncall-bot has an entry.

sec-oncall-bot: Alert: partner-sa-exposed. Snapshot: gs://redwood-audit/snapshots/1712223600.json. Rule: kms-wrapper-detected.

marie: for re-encrypting external blobs, here's a rough script snippet we can use (will wrap in infra tooling):
```bash
# create new key
gcloud kms keyrings create partner-rollover --location=global || true
gcloud kms keys create partner-rollover-key --location=global --keyring=partner-rollover --purpose=encryption
# decrypt old -> encrypt with new
OLD=$(base64 --decode <<< "ABCD...xyz==")
echo "$OLD" > /tmp/old.bin
gcloud kms decrypt --location=global --keyring=partner --key=partner-wrap --ciphertext-file=/tmp/old.bin --plaintext-file=/tmp/plain
gcloud kms encrypt --location=global --keyring=partner-rollover --key=partner-rollover-key --plaintext-file=/tmp/plain --ciphertext-file=/tmp/new.enc
NEW_CT=$(base64 -w0 /tmp/new.enc)
# upload to partner or update Vault
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d "{\"ciphertext\":\"$NEW_CT\"}" https://partner.example.com/replace
```

josh: if partner doesn't have a secure upload flow, we should push to a temporary signed URL and instruct them to fetch once. avoid email attachments.

liam: RBAC tightening: proposal to add an IAM Condition temporarily that restricts the exposed SA from being used outside our maintenance CIDRs and to disallow key decrypt until partner confirms rotation. example condition snippet provided in ticket.

olivia: applied conditional deny for 72h: `resource.name.startsWith('projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/partner') && not(request.auth.claims.ip in maintenance_range)` -> deny decrypt. logged change.

marie: scanning results: found 3 packages in partner S3 prefixes with the blob and 2 GH packages in partner org that reference the SA. opened PRs to block further downloads.

ryan: proceeding with rewrap flows. will coordinate a short maintenance window with partner for key rollover. planning for tonight 02:00 UTC.

josh: CI/GH secrets: create a sweep job to replace secrets in repo settings and rotate any deploy tokens. use GH API to list actions/secrets where the SA email shows up. marie, can you take that?

marie: taking GH/CI rotation. starting token revocation for suspicious tokens.

liam: forensics: check KMS access logs for Decrypt calls from the SA in last 30 days and look for unusual IPs or service accounts. also check our egress logs for large outgoing transfers.

olivia: audit note: exported KMS + IAM Admin logs to gs://redwood-audit/forensics/171222. snapshot saved.

sec-oncall-bot: Forensics export complete: gs://redwood-audit/forensics/171222/exports.tar.gz.

ryan: update 1712226300 - partner confirmed window. executing re-encrypt and replacing wrapped blobs. will update when Vault writes and GH secret patches finish.

ryan: update 1712227000 - re-encrypt done, uploaded to partner signed URL, Vault transit rewrap completed for internal items, CI secrets rotated. smoke tests in partner preprod passing.

marie: performed post-change scans, no remaining references in our buckets. opened follow-up for automated scanning rules and a pre-commit hook to detect key paths in artifacts.

liam: I'll own the postmortem and a policy change: mandatory transit use for partner-wrapped secrets and weekly partner-scan job.

josh: also adding an infra rule to alert on high-priv SAs being wrapped in artifacts during CI builds.

olivia: closing loop — final audit snapshot at gs://redwood-audit/snapshots/1712227100.json and ticket linked. good work team. :heart:
